title: Deploy Spring Boot Application to AWS
question: Deploy Spring Boot application to AWS. Requirements: 1) Microservices architecture with 5 services, 2) PostgreSQL database, 3) Redis cache, 4) High availability, 5) Auto-scaling, 6) CI/CD pipeline, 7) Cost-effective solution. Discuss: using AWS Elastic Beanstalk for simple deployment or ECS/EKS for containerized deployment, containerizing Spring Boot apps with Docker (multi-stage builds for smaller images), pushing Docker images to Amazon ECR, deploying to ECS Fargate for serverless containers or EKS for Kubernetes orchestration, using Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic across services, implementing health checks for each service, using Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with Multi-AZ deployment for high availability, configuring read replicas for read-heavy workloads, using Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with cluster mode for high availability, implementing service discovery with AWS Cloud Map or ECS service discovery, storing configuration in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store or Secrets Manager, using environment variables for service configuration, implementing CI/CD pipeline with AWS CodePipeline or GitHub Actions, automating Docker builds and pushes to ECR, deploying to ECS/EKS with rolling updates, implementing auto-scaling with target tracking policies (CPU/memory utilization, request count), using AWS CloudWatch for monitoring and logging, implementing distributed tracing with AWS X-Ray, using VPC for network isolation with public and private subnets, placing services in private subnets, placing load balancers in public subnets, implementing security groups to control traffic, using IAM roles for service permissions, and optimizing costs with spot instances, right-sizing containers, and using savings plans.

title: Production Kubernetes Deployment
question: Deploy Java application to production Kubernetes cluster. Requirements: 1) Zero-downtime deployments, 2) Handle traffic spikes (auto-scale), 3) Separate dev, staging, prod environments, 4) Secrets management, 5) Resource limits, 6) Monitoring and logging, 7) Disaster recovery. Discuss: using namespaces to separate environments (dev, staging, prod), implementing RBAC for access control per namespace, containerizing application with Docker, creating Kubernetes Deployment manifest with replica count, resource requests and limits (CPU: 500m/1, Memory: 512Mi/1Gi), implementing readiness and liveness probes for health checks, using Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) to scale based on CPU/memory/custom metrics, implementing rolling update strategy (maxSurge: 1, maxUnavailable: 0) for zero downtime, using Kubernetes Service (ClusterIP for internal, LoadBalancer for external), implementing Ingress for routing with TLS termination, using cert-manager for automatic TLS certificate management, storing secrets in Kubernetes Secrets or external secret management (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager), using ConfigMaps for non-sensitive configuration, implementing init containers for database migrations, using StatefulSets for stateful services (databases), provisioning PersistentVolumes with StorageClass for data persistence, implementing pod disruption budgets to maintain availability during updates, using node affinity and pod anti-affinity for high availability, deploying monitoring stack (Prometheus for metrics, Grafana for dashboards), implementing log aggregation with ELK stack or Loki, using distributed tracing with Jaeger, implementing GitOps with ArgoCD for declarative deployments, implementing backup strategy with Velero for disaster recovery, using network policies to restrict pod communication, and implementing multi-zone deployment for high availability.

title: Multi-Cloud Deployment Strategy
question: Implement multi-cloud deployment strategy. Requirements: 1) Deploy to AWS and Azure, 2) Avoid vendor lock-in, 3) Consistent deployment process, 4) Disaster recovery across clouds, 5) Cost optimization, 6) Unified monitoring. Discuss: using Terraform for infrastructure as code to provision resources across multiple clouds with consistent configuration, abstracting cloud-specific resources with Terraform modules, using Kubernetes as container orchestration platform across clouds (EKS on AWS, AKS on Azure) for consistent deployment experience, containerizing all applications for portability, using Helm charts for Kubernetes deployments with environment-specific values, implementing service mesh (Istio, Linkerd) for consistent traffic management and security across clusters, using multi-cluster service mesh for cross-cloud communication, implementing database replication across clouds for disaster recovery, using cloud-agnostic services where possible (Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, Redis), avoiding proprietary services that lock to specific cloud, implementing unified monitoring with Prometheus and Grafana deployed in each cloud, aggregating metrics to central location, using OpenTelemetry for standardized observability, implementing cost monitoring for both clouds with tools like CloudHealth or native billing APIs, using automated cost optimization (right-sizing, spot instances), implementing disaster recovery with active-passive or active-active setup, using DNS-based failover (Route 53, Azure Traffic Manager) to switch between clouds, implementing CI/CD pipeline that deploys to both clouds in parallel or sequentially, using feature flags to control rollout per cloud, implementing infrastructure testing to verify consistency across clouds, and using cloud-agnostic secret management (HashiCorp Vault).

title: Deploy Java Application Serverless
question: Deploy Java application using serverless architecture. Requirements: 1) Event-driven processing, 2) REST API, 3) Cost optimization for variable load, 4) Fast cold start, 5) Integration with managed services. Discuss: using AWS Lambda for serverless compute with Java runtime, optimizing Java application for Lambda (reduce dependencies, use lightweight frameworks like Micronaut or Quarkus instead of Spring Boot for faster cold start), implementing Lambda functions for API endpoints with API Gateway integration, using Lambda proxy integration for REST API, implementing CORS and authentication (Lambda authorizers or Cognito), deploying Lambda functions in VPC to access RDS/ElastiCache if needed, using Lambda Layers for shared dependencies to reduce deployment package size, implementing asynchronous processing with Lambda triggered by SQS, SNS, or EventBridge, using Lambda with S3 triggers for file processing, storing data in DynamoDB for serverless database or RDS Proxy for connection pooling with RDS, implementing caching with API Gateway caching or Lambda@Edge for CloudFront, using CloudWatch Logs for logging with log retention policies, implementing Lambda provisioned concurrency for critical functions to avoid cold start, using Lambda reserved concurrency to control scaling and costs, implementing dead letter queues for failed invocations, using AWS SAM or Serverless Framework for deployment automation, implementing CI/CD with CodePipeline or GitHub Actions, optimizing costs with Lambda power tuning to find optimal memory/CPU configuration, using Step Functions for complex workflows, implementing distributed tracing with X-Ray, and monitoring Lambda metrics (invocations, duration, errors, throttles) in CloudWatch.
